# Focused research fixture — fictional evidence

All companies, people, prices and source pages in this fixture are invented test data. Use only this supplied evidence; do not browse, call GooseWorks or spend. The test date is 22 October 2026. Setup, source reads and approval state are simulated, not live acceptance. Relative file citations refer to supplied evidence, not public verification.

## Brand / product source — supplied product sheet, checked 22 Oct

Papertrail is an invoice-exception review tool. It has a shared review queue, a CSV review-history export and a recorded reviewer decision. It keeps existing human approvals. It does not automatically pay invoices or write back into an ERP. It has no certified compliance claim or documented time-saved result. Its current brand position is “fully automatic accounts payable”. Brand voice is confirmed: plain, specific, no superlatives. Team plan: $120/month for up to five reviewers; tax excluded. Hero product: the review queue.

## Rival source — supplied BillPilot pricing/product captures, 22 Oct

BillPilot describes itself as “Accounts payable from intake to payment”. It supports native ERP write-back and payment execution. Its review history is available on its Enterprise tier; the supplied capture does not show an export format or Enterprise price. Standard is $25/reviewer/month, minimum ten seats, taxes excluded. Annual discounts and migration services are unknown. The five-reviewer comparison therefore costs $250/month for Standard, but history/export parity cannot be priced from the supplied sheet.

## Buyer groups / owner win-loss notes — supplied interview notes, 19 Oct

Primary: controllers at multi-entity businesses whose invoice exceptions need an accountable review before approval. Five interviews; three explicitly want a record they can hand to a finance reviewer. One said “I need to see who decided, not another score”. Secondary: AP team leads handing disputed invoices between staff; three interviews; one said “The next person asks me what happened, every time”. Both use an ERP and keep its approvals.

Actual deal notes: two prospects chose a manual review pilot because they wanted to keep their approvals. One prospect stayed with BillPilot because native ERP write-back was essential. These observations are a tiny deal sample, not win-rate evidence.

Objection excerpts: “We already use BillPilot.” “Is this another approval system?” “Why not use a spreadsheet?” The last buyer described searching email for the reviewer decision; no measured time or error result was captured.

## Approvals — simulated owner, 22 Oct

Owner says: “Approve these exact product lines for this test: Review invoice exceptions in a shared queue. Export the review history as CSV. Keep your existing approval steps.”

Owner says: “Approve this dated, price-only comparison: For five reviewers, Papertrail is $120/month; BillPilot Standard is $250/month because it requires ten seats. This does not compare Enterprise features.”

No approval for “faster”, “cheaper for everyone”, “compliant”, “fully automatic”, or a time-saved claim. No positioning option has been selected. No sending or publishing is requested.
